problem:
Title: Factorial Divides Product of Successive Numbers

Let $m, n \in \N_{\ge 1}$ be [[Definition:Natural Numbers|natural numbers]]

Let $m^{\overline n}$ be [[Definition:Rising Factorial|$m$ to the power of $n$ rising]].

Then:

:$m^{\overline n} \equiv 0 \bmod n!$

That is, the [[Definition:Factorial|factorial]] of $n$ [[Definition:Divisor of Integer|divides]] the product of $n$ successive numbers.
proof_numbered:
0001 | Let $m \in \N_{\ge 1}$.
0002 | 
0003 | Consider the [[Definition:Set|set]]:
0004 | 
0005 | :$S = \set{m, m + 1, m + 2, \ldots, m + n - 1}$
0006 | 
0007 | Note $S$ has $n$ [[Definition:Element|elements]].
0008 | 
0009 | By [[Set of Successive Numbers contains Unique Multiple]]:
0010 | 
0011 | :$\set m$ contains a [[Definition:Factor (Algebra)|factor]] of $1$
0012 | 
0013 | :$\set {m, m + 1}$ contains a [[Definition:Factor (Algebra)|factor]] of $2$
0014 | 
0015 | and in general:
0016 | 
0017 | :$\set {m, m + 1, \ldots, m + j - 1}$ contains a [[Definition:Factor (Algebra)|factor]] of $j$.
0018 | 
0019 | It follows that $S$ contains factors of $1, 2, 3, \ldots, n$.
0020 | 
0021 | Multiplying all elements of $S$ gives:
0022 | 
0023 | {{begin-eqn}}
0024 | {{eqn | l = m \paren {m + 1} \dotsm \paren {m + n - 1}
0025 |       | r = k_1 2 k_2 3 k_3 \dotsm \paren {n - 1} k_{n - 1} n k_n
0026 |       | c = for some $k_1, k_2, \ldots, k_n \in N$
0027 | }}
0028 | {{eqn | r = \paren {k_1 k_2 \dotsm k_{n - 1} k_n} \paren {1 \times 2 \times \dotsm \times \paren {n - 1} \times n}
0029 | }}
0030 | {{eqn | ll= \leadsto
0031 |       | l = m^{\overline n}
0032 |       | r = K n!
0033 |       | c = for some $K \in \N$
0034 | }}
0035 | {{eqn | ll= \leadsto
0036 |       | l = m^{\overline n}
0037 |       | o = \equiv
0038 |       | r = 0 \bmod n!
0039 | }}
0040 | {{end-eqn}}
0041 | {{qed}}
